title: Fit the left-hand and right-hand hinge brackets each to the pocket that takes its hand
instruction: Fit a hinge bracket into each of the two pockets in the frame, seated flat.
context: Handed parts (hinge brackets, door closers, mirror housings) look alike, and fitting the wrong hand is a classic assembly error. Done by: team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092.00), cabinetmakers (51-7011.00). The fixture is mistake-proof: the wrong hand will not seat. Unlike accepted TK-TPC59R, where size picks the part, and TK-SMQ69N (build a model's mirror image), these parts differ only as mirror images; the skill is finding the right hand without forcing parts.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart): 'in front' is away from the arm bases, left and right are the robot's, heights are above the table top. Frame bar (fixed, grey steel, 6.0 cm front to back, 32 cm long side to side, 2.0 cm tall) from 30.0 to 36.0 cm in front, centred on the midline. Two pockets in its top, each 4.9 cm front to back, 7.4 cm side to side and 0.8 cm deep (floor 1.2 cm above the table), centred 33.0 cm in front and 10.0 cm left and 10.0 cm right of the midline. In each pocket a dark steel peg, 1.4 x 1.4 cm and 0.6 cm tall, stands in one far corner, touching both walls: the far-left corner of the left pocket, the far-right corner of the right pocket. Three hinge brackets (loose, grey aluminium, 80 g each): a base plate 6.6 cm long, 4.1 cm wide and 0.8 cm thick with a 2.0 x 2.0 cm square notch cut from one corner, and an upright leg 0.8 cm thick and 3.0 cm tall (top 3.8 cm above the base's underside) along the long edge next to the notch, running from the notch to the other end (4.6 cm). Left-hand bracket: seen from above with the leg on the far side, the notch is at the left end. Right-hand bracket: the mirror image, notch at the right end. Lot A (the screenshot): the brackets lie flat on the table, long side across the table, legs on the far side, centred 21.0 cm in front: the left-hand one on the midline, a right-hand one 11.0 cm left of the midline, the other right-hand one 11.0 cm right. Nothing else is on the table. Lot B: the left-hand bracket at 11.0 cm left and a right-hand one on the midline. Lot C: the left-hand bracket at 11.0 cm right, turned a quarter turn so its leg is on the robot's left; the right-hand brackets on the midline and at 11.0 cm left, each turned a quarter turn the other way, legs on the robot's right. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end from a photo, a ruler and the video. A bracket is seated in a pocket when it lies flat on the pocket floor: its base's underside within 1 mm of the floor at all four corners (within 2 degrees of level), the whole base inside the pocket, and the pocket's peg standing in the bracket's notch, not under its base. A bracket that is the wrong hand, or turned the wrong way, rests on the peg about 6 mm proud and tilted, and is not seated. Released means no part of either gripper body or its fingertips within 5 mm of any bracket; still means every bracket moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s. Score 1.0: both pockets have a seated bracket, released and still for 2 s. Score 0.5: the left pocket has a seated bracket (only the left-hand one fits it) and the right pocket has none seated, released and still; a bracket resting proud in the right pocket does not change this. Score 0 in every other case: only the right pocket seated, the left pocket empty or its bracket proud on the peg, anything held or moving. Possible scores per trial: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Lay the three brackets flat on the table 21.0 cm in front, long side across the table. Lot A: left-hand on the midline, right-hand brackets at 11.0 cm left and 11.0 cm right, all legs on the far side. Lot B: left-hand at 11.0 cm left, right-hand on the midline and at 11.0 cm right, legs on the far side. Lot C: left-hand at 11.0 cm right with its leg on the robot's left; right-hand on the midline and at 11.0 cm left with legs on the robot's right. The frame is fixed. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes: no hinge knuckle or screw holes, and the pegs stand in for a fixture's locating pins. The pockets have 4 mm of play per side. Default simulator friction. Release uses the simulator's finger shapes. A robot could also find the left-hand bracket by trying each one in the left pocket. Three lots move it, which stops a fixed habit but not a memorised replay of all three layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
